# Lab 17.5: Differential Privacy

## What We Are Going to Do
Protect a view with a differential privacy rule and run queries that add statistical noise, with a limited privacy budget.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a view with a differential privacy policy.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW lab17_dcr.orders_dp
OPTIONS (privacy_policy = '''{
  "differential_privacy_policy": {
    "privacy_unit_column": "user_id",
    "max_epsilon_per_query": 1.0,
    "epsilon_budget": 5.0,
    "delta_per_query": 1e-7,
    "delta_budget": 1e-5,
    "max_groups_contributed": 1
  }}''')
AS SELECT o.user_id, u.country, o.num_of_item
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders` o
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON u.id = o.user_id;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Run a private query.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT WITH DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY
  OPTIONS (epsilon = 0.5, delta = 1e-7)
  country, COUNT(*) AS orders, AVG(num_of_item) AS avg_items
FROM lab17_dcr.orders_dp
GROUP BY country;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Run it again and compare.** The numbers change slightly each time. That noise is what protects individuals.

4. **[SQL] Use up the budget.** Run the query several more times. Once the total epsilon spent passes `5.0`, BigQuery refuses further queries on the view.

5. **[Console] Discuss epsilon.** Smaller epsilon = more noise = more privacy. Larger epsilon = more accurate = less privacy.

6. **[CLI] Run a private query from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT WITH DIFFERENTIAL_PRIVACY OPTIONS (epsilon = 0.5, delta = 1e-7) country, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM lab17_dcr.orders_dp GROUP BY country'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Noise | Results vary slightly per run |
| Epsilon | Privacy cost per query |
| Budget | Queries blocked when exhausted |
| Rows | One user counts in at most one group |
